c74object.name: syncSuite.score.server
c74object.digest: Node-for-Max server that streams a page-turning score to one or more remote devices.
c74object.description: Use it to serve a page-turning PDF score to remote devices (phones, tablets, stand-mounted screens) over the network, one "score" per device.

objarg.name: port
objarg.description: Sets the @port attribute at creation time, e.g. "syncSuite.score.server 8111". Optional; defaults to 8111 if omitted.

inlet.digest: Commands controlling the server process and its registered scores
inlet.description: Accepts server-level commands ("start", "stop", "install", "addScore", "deleteScore", "get", "restart", "refresh", "all") as well as messages addressed to a specific score, in the form "<scoreName> <command> <args...>". See the Messages section for the full list.

outlet.digest: Reports whether the HTTP/WebSocket server is running
outlet.description: Outputs "serverState 1" once the server is listening, and "serverState 0" if it stops or fails to start.

outlet.digest: Every other report from the server
outlet.description: Everything the server reports other than "serverState": "ip <address>:<port>" once listening, "error"/"warning" messages, the current page ("<scoreName> currentPage <n>", whenever it changes — from "addScore", "page", "load"/"read", "restart", or a device turning its own page) and page count ("<scoreName> pages <n>" — reported right after "addScore" as 0, and right after "load"/"read" from the PDF file itself, without needing any device connected; 0 again after "restart"; and again whenever any connected device separately reports its own rendered count back), device connect/disconnect and info reports ("deviceEvent"/"deviceInfo"), the "<scoreName> connectedDevices"/"<scoreName> state" health messages, the score's full URL after "addScore" or "load"/"read" (once the server is running), "<scoreName> timerValue <seconds>" after "timer" and once per second while it's running, and replies to "get". See the Messages section for the full list.

method.name: start
method.description: Launches the underlying node.script, which starts the HTTP/WebSocket server on the configured @port.

method.name: stop
method.description: Shuts down the running server, disconnecting any connected devices.

method.name: install
method.digest: Installs the server's Node dependencies (express, ws, pdf-lib)
method.description: Runs "npm install express ws pdf-lib" for the node.script. Only needs to be sent once, the first time the object is used, or after the node_modules folder has been removed.

method.name: addScore
method.description: Creates a new score identified by "name" (e.g. "violin"). Once added, the score can be reached by remote devices at "/<name>" and can be addressed directly with "<name> <command> <args...>" messages, see below. Replies with "<name> currentPage 1" and "<name> pages 0" (nothing is loaded yet); if the server is already running, also replies with "<name> address <address>:<port>/<name>" — the full URL devices should open to view this score.

method.name: deleteScore
method.description: Deletes the score "name" and disconnects any devices currently viewing it.

method.name: rename
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> rename <new-name>". Renames that score to "new-name" — its loaded PDF, page, and all other state carry over unchanged, as do its currently connected devices: each one is told in place to reconnect under the new name (no full page reload, no re-tapping the fullscreen gate). Any future message must address the score by its new name, e.g. "<new-name> page 2". Fails if "new-name" is already in use by another score. Replies the same way "addScore" would, posted under the new name: "<new-name> renamed <new-name>", "<new-name> currentPage <n>", "<new-name> pages <n>", "<new-name> connectedDevices <n>" and "<new-name> state 1|0", and — if the server is already running — "<new-name> address <address>:<port>/<new-name>".

method.name: get
method.digest: Reports a score's address, loaded file, page and connected devices
method.description:
Requests information about the score "name". The server replies with, prefixed by that score's name:
- "<name> ip <address>:<port>/<name>": the full URL path devices should open to view this score.
- "<name> file <absolute-path>": the currently loaded PDF's path, or an empty string if none is loaded.
- "<name> currentPage <n>": the current page.
- "<name> pages <n>": the total page count of the loaded PDF (0 if none loaded).
- "<name> connectedDevices <device-ip> 1": one such message per device currently connected to this score, giving that device's IP address.
Fails if the server isn't running or "name" isn't a registered score.

method.name: restart
method.digest: Resets every score to its default state
method.description: Resets all registered scores' state and reloads every currently connected device. Sent as "<scoreName> restart" instead, it resets only that one score, and replies with "<scoreName> currentPage 1" and "<scoreName> pages 0".

method.name: refresh
method.description: Forces every connected device's viewer page to reload, without changing any state. Sent as "<scoreName> refresh" instead, it reloads only that score's connected devices.

method.name: all
method.digest: Sends a score command to every registered score
method.description: Fans a per-score command (see below) out to every currently registered score, e.g. "all page 1" turns every score to page 1.

method.name: load
method.digest: Loads a PDF file for a score
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> load <absolute-path>". Loads the PDF at "path" for that score, resets it to page 1, and pushes it to every connected device. The path must be absolute; a relative path is used as-is and a warning is posted, since it will typically fail to resolve on the Node side. A leading boot-volume prefix from macOS "Copy as Pathname" (e.g. "Macintosh HD:/Users/...") is stripped automatically. "read" is an alias for this message. Replies immediately with "<scoreName> currentPage 1", followed a moment later by "<scoreName> pages <n>" — the server reads the real page count directly from the PDF file itself, no connected device required. If the server is already running, also replies with "<scoreName> address <address>:<port>/<scoreName>" — the full URL devices should open to view this score.

method.name: page
method.digest: Turns a score to the given page
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> page <n>". Turns to page "n" (1-based) on every connected device, and replies with "<scoreName> currentPage <n>".

method.name: bar
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> bar <n>". Updates the bar shown by that score's bar/beat indicator (see "displayBar").

method.name: beat
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> beat <n>". Updates the beat shown by that score's bar/beat indicator (see "displayBeat") and the number shown inside the metronome circle (see "displayMetronome").

method.name: position
method.digest: Sets a score's current bar and beat together
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> position <bar> <beat>". Equivalent to sending "bar" and "beat" separately, but as a single message/broadcast — prefer this over two separate calls when driving continuous playback position, to halve the network and redraw overhead.

method.name: displayBar
method.digest: Shows or hides a score's bar indicator
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> displayBar <0/1>". Shows (1) or hides (0) the current-bar readout on that score's connected devices.

method.name: displayBeat
method.digest: Shows or hides a score's beat indicator
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> displayBeat <0/1>". Shows (1) or hides (0) the current-beat readout on that score's connected devices.

method.name: barBeatPosition
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> barBeatPosition <x> <y>". Places the bar/beat readout at the normalized float (0.-1.) position x, y on the screen.

method.name: barColor
method.digest: Sets the bar readout's text color
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> barColor <r> <g> <b>", each 0-255. Sets the color of the "Bar <n>" text in the bar/beat readout (see "displayBar"). Default green (0 255 0). Out-of-range values are clamped; fewer than 3 numbers leaves the color unchanged.

method.name: beatColor
method.digest: Sets the beat readout's text color
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> beatColor <r> <g> <b>", each 0-255. Sets the color of the "Beat <n>" text in the bar/beat readout (see "displayBeat"). Default green (0 255 0). Out-of-range values are clamped; fewer than 3 numbers leaves the color unchanged.

method.name: barSize
method.digest: Sets the bar readout's text size
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> barSize <n>". Sets the font size, in pixels, of the "Bar <n>" text in the bar/beat readout (see "displayBar"). Default 22. If the readout would overflow the screen at that size, the viewer shrinks it (and "beatSize") together to fit rather than clipping.

method.name: beatSize
method.digest: Sets the beat readout's text size
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> beatSize <n>". Sets the font size, in pixels, of the "Beat <n>" text in the bar/beat readout (see "displayBeat"). Default 22. If the readout would overflow the screen at that size, the viewer shrinks it (and "barSize") together to fit rather than clipping.

method.name: text
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> text <string>". Displays "string" as an overlay message on that score's connected devices.

method.name: textSize
method.digest: Sets a score's overlay text size
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> textSize <n>". Sets the font size, in points, of that score's overlay text.

method.name: textPosition
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> textPosition <x> <y>". Places the overlay text at the normalized float (0.-1.) position x, y on the screen.

method.name: textColor
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> textColor <r> <g> <b>", each 0-255. Sets the color of the overlay text (see "text"). Default white (255 255 255). Out-of-range values are clamped; fewer than 3 numbers leaves the color unchanged.

method.name: black
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> black <0/1>". Blacks out (1) or restores (0) that score's score display on every connected device. Any nonzero value counts as on, e.g. "black 2".

method.name: zoom
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> zoom <factor>". Scales that score by "factor" (1.0 is normal size).

method.name: flash
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> flash". Flashes that score's screen in its current flashColor, for its current flashDuration (default 50ms). One-shot, not persisted in the score's state.

method.name: flashColor
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> flashColor <r> <g> <b>", each 0-255. Sets the color used the next time "flash" is sent to that score; does not flash by itself. Default red (255 0 0). Out-of-range values are clamped; fewer than 3 numbers leaves the color unchanged.

method.name: flashDuration
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> flashDuration <ms>". Sets how long, in milliseconds, the next "flash" sent to that score stays visible; does not flash by itself. Default 50.

method.name: backgroundColor
method.digest: Sets a score's page background color
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> backgroundColor <r> <g> <b>", each 0-255. Sets the background color behind that score's page. Out-of-range values are clamped; fewer than 3 numbers leaves the color unchanged.

method.name: invertColor
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> invertColor <0/1>". Enables (1) or disables (0) color inversion of that score's display.

method.name: displayMetronome
method.digest: Shows or hides a score's on-screen metronome
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> displayMetronome <0/1>". Shows (1) or hides (0) the on-screen metronome on that score's connected devices. The metronome is a circle that briefly flashes white on every "beat" (or "position") update, showing the current beat number inside it.

method.name: metronomeSize
method.digest: Sets the size of a score's on-screen metronome
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> metronomeSize <n>". Scales the on-screen metronome shown on that score's connected devices.

method.name: metronomeColor
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> metronomeColor <r> <g> <b>", each 0-255. Sets the metronome circle's color between beats; it always flashes white on the beat itself. Default dark gray (51 51 51). Out-of-range values are clamped; fewer than 3 numbers leaves the color unchanged.

method.name: metronomePosition
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> metronomePosition <x> <y>". Places the metronome circle at the normalized float (0.-1.) position x, y on the screen. Default near the top-right corner.

method.name: timer
method.digest: Starts, sets, or resets a score's on-screen timer
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> timer" (starts/restarts the timer running), "<scoreName> timer <n>" (sets that score's timer target to "n" seconds, then starts running the same way), or "<scoreName> timer reset" (stops the timer and resets it, without changing the target set by the last "timer <n>"). If "timerDirection" is 1 (default), the timer counts up from 00:00 and, once a target has been set, stops once it reaches it; if "timerDirection" is -1, the timer counts down from the target to 00:00 and stops there. Replies with "<scoreName> timerValue <seconds>". While running, the server ticks the timer once per second and broadcasts the new value to every connected device, rendered there in mm:ss format (see "timerDisplay").

method.name: timerDisplay
method.digest: Shows or hides a score's on-screen timer
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> timerDisplay <0/1>". Shows (1) or hides (0) the timer (see "timer") on that score's connected devices.

method.name: timerSize
method.digest: Sets a score's timer text size
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> timerSize <n>". Sets the font size, in points, of that score's timer readout. Default 48.

method.name: timerColor
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> timerColor <r> <g> <b>", each 0-255. Sets the color of the timer readout (see "timer"). Default white (255 255 255). Out-of-range values are clamped; fewer than 3 numbers leaves the color unchanged.

method.name: timerDirection
method.digest: Sets whether a score's timer counts up or down

method.name: timerPosition
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> timerPosition <x> <y>". Places the timer readout at the normalized float (0.-1.) position x, y on the screen. Default near top-center.

method.name: allowPageChange
method.digest: Allows or blocks a device from turning its own pages
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> allowPageChange <0/1>". When enabled (1), a device may turn that score's pages itself (e.g. by tapping/swiping); when disabled (0), page turns from the device are ignored and pages can only be changed from Max with "page". A device's own page turns are also always bounded by the score's page count — see "<scoreName> pages <n>" on outlet 1, sent moments after "load"/"read" resolves it from the PDF file — so they have no effect in the brief window before that arrives.

method.name: getDeviceInfo
method.description: Sent as "<scoreName> getDeviceInfo". Asks every device currently connected to that score to report its screen size, pixel ratio and fullscreen state back to Max.

attribute.name: port
attribute.description: HTTP/WebSocket port used when the server (re)starts. Default 8111. Takes effect only at launch time — set it before sending "start", or set it as a creation argument; there is currently no message to change the port of an already-running server.

attribute.name: watch
attribute.digest: Auto-reloads the server when its script file changes
attribute.description: When enabled (1), the Node process is automatically restarted whenever syncSuite.score.server.js is edited and saved on disk. The configured port and registered scores are resent to it after each reload. Default 1.
